rationale: Start with a broad, mid-length scouting gradient at moderate temperature to maximize the chance all 10 compounds elute while revealing the overall retention window and where the critical pairs lie. This gives a useful first map without being so slow that the initial CRF is unnecessarily penalized.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only available gain is reducing t_last. Keep composition and temperature fixed and shorten the gradient one step to test how much time can be saved before any pair drops below full-resolution credit.

The current method is very close to the 10 min target and the limiting pair has only just remained above full-credit resolution, so the next best move is one more reduction in gradient time. This directly tests whether we can bring the last peak under 10 min while keeping the worst pair at or above R = 1.5.

At 14 min the run is fast enough, and the only problem is the 6/7 pair falling below full resolution credit. Lowering temperature by one step should increase retention selectivity and spacing more gently than lengthening the gradient, giving a chance to restore that pair while keeping t_last under 10 min.

Lowering temperature hurt selectivity, so probe the opposite direction at the same fast gradient. A 5 C increase may improve the critical mid-cluster selectivity enough to recover full-credit resolution while keeping the last peak comfortably under 10 min.

Temperature changes worsened the critical cluster, so keep 40 C and adjust gradient shape instead. Lowering phi1 one step should make the late part of the gradient shallower near the problematic mid-eluting region, potentially increasing the 6/7 spacing while still likely keeping all compounds under 10 min.

Dropping phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved the limiting 6/7 pair while keeping t_last below 10 min, so continue one more step in the same direction. This should further flatten the late gradient and may push that pair to full-credit resolution, with only a modest risk of moving the last peak slightly past 10 min.

At phi1 = 0.85 the resolution is fully restored but the run is slightly too long, while phi1 = 0.90 is just under 10 min but a bit short on the 6/7 pair. Shortening tG at phi1 = 0.90 tests whether a steeper gradient can pull t_last down enough while preserving more of the favorable selectivity than the 0.95 endpoint did.

The 14 min runs show a clear tradeoff: phi1 = 0.85 gives full resolution but is slightly too slow, while phi1 = 0.90 is faster but under-resolves 6/7. Testing phi1 = 0.85 at 12 min checks whether shortening the run by one step can keep the critical pair at full credit while bringing t_last closer to or under 10 min.

The persistent bottleneck is the dense mid-eluting cluster rather than the late peak, so changing the starting strength is a good next lever. Raising phi0 one step should compress the earliest region while altering how the cluster experiences the gradient, potentially improving the 6/7 selectivity without the time penalty seen when only lowering phi1.

You have reached the apparent optimum boundary: full resolution with t_last essentially at 10 min. The next move is to shorten tG one step from this winning method to see whether the last peak can be pulled just below 10 min while retaining all pairs at R >= 1.5.

The winning method sits exactly on the time limit with comfortable resolution margin, while shortening tG lost the 6/7 pair. Lowering phi1 one step from the optimum should preserve or improve the critical pair and may shift the last peak just under 10 min without sacrificing full-credit resolution.

Lowering phi1 from the optimum increased retention too much, so test the opposite side of the local optimum. Raising phi1 one step may pull t_last just below 10 min, and with the current method's resolution margin of 1.61 there is a reasonable chance the critical pair still stays at or above 1.5.

The composition optimum is very tight around the current best method, so the remaining chance to beat it is a small temperature tweak from that exact composition. Raising T by 5 C may reduce t_last just enough below 10 min while hopefully keeping the critical 6/7 pair above the 1.5 threshold.

The 45 C move strongly worsened the 6/7 selectivity, so check the opposite temperature direction from the best composition instead of further disturbing gradient shape. This new best method has full resolution with extra time margin, so the right exploitation move is to shorten tG one step. That tests whether the run can be made even faster while keeping the critical 6/7 pair above the R = 1.5 threshold.

Testing phi1 = 0.80 at phi0 = 0.15 explores whether the stronger beneficial effect of higher phi0 can offset the extra retention from a lower phi1, potentially retaining full resolution while staying under 10 min.

At phi0 = 0.15, lowering phi1 to 0.80 preserved resolution but pushed t_last above 10 min, so the symmetric test at phi1 = 0.90 is the most informative remaining composition move. It may keep the critical pair above 1.5 while giving a faster method than the current top-scoring settings.

A key remaining gap is the unexplored combination of lower phi1 with the shorter 12 min gradient at the successful phi0 = 0.10 setting. This tests whether combining the faster high-phi0 effect with the stronger low-phi1 resolution effect can recover full-credit separation and provide another robust optimum candidate.

The phi0 = 0.20, phi1 = 0.80 method reached CRF 1.000 with good time margin, so one final outward step in phi0 is the best chance to identify an even faster fully resolved edge.
